REFUTED. The premise 'the v0.717 payload has 6 pages with completely different wording' is false, and its supporting inference is a non sequitur. payload.xml IS the same SWF as shs3_payload — the obfuscated class name '1t7924s0' appears in it at lines 113188 and 2653462, and that class declares [Embed(source="/_assets/assets.swf", symbol="symbol756")] at :7, i.e. the very DefineSpriteTag at payload.xml:528088 that immediately follows the six war-rules title/body pairs (characterIDs 744-755 at :528040-528084). That class sets max:int = 7 at :23 and has a case 7 at :121-123 pulling getString(11016)/(11017). It overwrites warrulestitle.text and warruleswords.text from getString() on EVERY page turn, so the '1/6'..'6/6' DefineEditText strings are dead authoring placeholders — exactly the trap the sibling claim rank-ladder-a1-confirmed correctly flags in ui_strings.txt. The claim's own reasoning gives it away: 'grep room rules over shs3_payload/scripts returns nothing' is expected, because v0.717 streams its strings (§1t1521s0§.as:5-6 URLLoader/URLRequest). The frame's 1/7 does not contradict v0.717 — it CONFIRMS it. No frame-vs-artifact conflict exists here, the 'caps meta-social below 78' conclusion is unearned, and the crop the claim states, (60,20)-(300,45), cannot contain the body text it quotes (the body lines sit near y=58 and y=82 in a 512x288 frame).

Exact. :5 'import flash.net.URLLoader;' and :6 'import flash.net.URLRequest;' sit in the class that declares 'public static function getString(param1:int, param2:Array = null) : String' at :122. setLanguage prints 'Loading language data...' at :47 and :60, and the fetch itself is at :228-229 'new URLLoader() ... load(new URLRequest(filename))'. The Android LangManager imports neither. This is the structural reason no v0.717 string table exists on disk, why ids 11016/11017/11496 resolve to nothing, and why the Android-vs-web string caveat is permanent.

new_findings.text: Static DefineEditText copy inside reference/extracted/payload.xml is AUTHORING PLACEHOLDER, not shipped v0.717 UI copy, for every field LangManager writes to at runtime. The war-rules dialog proves it: payload.xml:528040-528084 embeds six title/body pairs reading 'War room rules 1/6'..'6/6' (characterIDs 744-755), and the DefineSpriteTag that owns them is spriteId 756 at :528088 — which is precisely the symbol the shipping class embeds ([Embed(symbol="symbol756")] at §1t7924s0§.as:7). That class declares max:int = 7 (:23) and overwrites warrulestitle.text / warruleswords.text from getString() on every page turn (:96-123, case 7 at :121-123). This is the same class of trap as ui_strings.txt:215's 'soldier ... 15/60'. Treat payload.xml static text as a dead draft unless no code writes that field.
new_findings.quote: §1t7924s0§.as:7 [Embed(source="/_assets/assets.swf", symbol="symbol756")] · :23 internal var max:int = 7; · :121-123 case 7: this.warrulestitle.text = §1t1521s0§.getString(11016); this.warruleswords.text = §1t1521s0§.getString(11017);  ||  payload.xml:528040 initialText "War room rules 1/6  (joining a battle)" characterID="744" · :528088 <item type="DefineSpriteTag" frameCount="6" spriteId="756">
new_findings.lane_impact: L0 meta-social and every lane porting UI copy — this is what kills the 'the filmed build is neither artifact' reading, and it is the general rule that prevents the next agent from porting a 6-page rulebook, 'soldier' rank, or '/60' move cap out of a placeholder.

new_findings.text: The web-only weight term §1t478s0§ that makes the sell-price input diverge from Android is NOT unresolved: it is the payload of modifier id 208. §1t17s0§.as declares three non-stat modifier ids Android lacks, not one — 206 (xp), 207 and 208 — and 208 carries §1t478s0§ into the save string and into the displayed Weight line. So the web weight shown to the player is (row weight + modifier-208 value), and getWeight() multiplies that sum by quantity.
new_findings.quote: :60 internal var §1t478s0§:int = 0; · :22 public static var §1t8741s0§:int = 208; · :300 _loc2_ += §1t8741s0§ + "@" + this.§1t478s0§ + "#"; · :1407 _loc3_ += §1t1521s0§.getString(139) + ": " + (_loc2_.weight + this.§1t478s0§) + "\n"; · :1974 return (this.weight + this.§1t478s0§) * this.§1t484s0§();
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 economy + L10 persistence — closes the PARTIAL on items-equipment/sell-weight-branch-is-stack-weight and adds ids 207 and 208 to the web save schema alongside the already-claimed 206.

new_findings.text: The 48 floor that kills the lone <slashusage>24</slashusage> row is applied TWICE, not once. Besides StatsManager.getSlashUsage(), XMLNpc.initDuelist() clamps the same value for every AI duelist. So 24 is unreachable for both the player and every NPC, and no path in either build can produce a slash budget below 48.
new_findings.lane_impact: L1 combat core — hardens items-equipment/slashusage-24-is-dead from 'dead on the player path' to 'dead everywhere'.

new_findings.text: The 12-frame retarget cadence is set by four classes, not one: MCSPlayer (EnemyPlayer's own base), EnemyPlayer, EnemyElite and FriendlyElite. Every Enemy* class that extends NPC directly — Archer, Katana, Knife, Ninja, Ogre, Shield, Spear, SpearElite, Zombie, Goblin, JiangSi, KanjiGuardian, NianMonster, SorcererBoss, TrainingDummy and the animal roster — inherits NPC.as:22's 24. The two-cadence model is right; 'only EnemyPlayer overrides it' is not.
new_findings.quote: NPC.as:22 internal var aiCounterMax:int = 24; · MCSPlayer.as:165 aiCounterMax = 12; · EnemyPlayer.as:52 aiCounterMax = 12; · EnemyElite.as:18 aiCounterMax = 12; · FriendlyElite.as:18 aiCounterMax = 12; · EnemyElite.as:3 public class EnemyElite extends EnemyPlayer · EnemyKnife.as:3 public class EnemyKnife extends NPC
new_findings.lane_impact: L-enemies-ai — an implementer wiring '24 for everything except EnemyPlayer' makes elites half as reactive as the original.

new_findings.text: 'ShopUI.as:401 is the sole call site of getSellAmt' is an ANDROID-only fact. The web v0.717 build has two: the shop slot (§1t6519s0§.as:474) and an accumulator at §1t6172s0§.as:417 that sums sell amounts across items. The no-shop-side-level-multiplier inference still stands, but it must be re-derived on the web build rather than inherited from the Android grep.
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 economy — a bulk-sell total exists in v0.717 that the Android-sourced survey has no row for.

new_findings.text: The one-hour war turn is confirmed on film by two consecutive frames, not one: seg-29 frame_0019 reads 'NEXT TURN IN 1:00:00' and frame_0020 reads 'NEXT TURN IN 59:58'. That brackets WARMOVEINTERVAL = 60*60 as a full-hour countdown that starts at exactly 1:00:00, which no single frame establishes.

new_findings.lane_impact: L0 meta-social — corrects the frame attribution in meta-social/rank-ladder-a1-confirmed and upgrades the turn timer from a decompile constant to a frame-confirmed countdown.

new_findings.text: The two war UIs do not use different hues for all four clans — only for two. Sides 1 and 4 are identical across both (0xFF0000 red, 0xFFFF00 yellow). Side 2 is #00FF00 in the territory map but 0x009900 in the hex UI, and side 3 is #00FFFF vs 0x0066FF. So the palette choice a renderer has to make is confined to the green and cyan clans.
new_findings.lane_impact: L-art + L0 meta-social — sharpens meta-social/side-to-clan-bound-in-code from 'the two UIs disagree' to exactly which two sides disagree.

new_findings.text: The enemy id the web survivalmode wave table adds and Android's drops is not an unresolvable number: npc 443 resolves to 'Soldier' in the already-parsed S0-3 table. The web-only late-wave additions are therefore fully named content, not a gap.
new_findings.quote: resolved_names.json npcdata.xml.resolved["443"] = {"name": "Soldier"}; web rows read <id>449|454|449|454|443</id> where android reads <id>449|454</id>
new_findings.lane_impact: L-enemies-ai — the web wave mix can be ported outright; nothing in the 14 divergent rows is blocked.
